cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Remember Me Correctly
cards.instruction: Create small tests of whether someone remembers your preferences, stories, or shared history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you caption our holiday photo, what did I say when we missed that boat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember you laughing. Not the words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll start you off: 'Well, that's the last time we trust...'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's try multiple choice. Your watch, my French, or the man selling us watches?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 blocks captioning for a recall test, A3 grants a clue and A5 substitutes multiple choice for B generic-caption request, making A authority govern the test format.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 remembers laughter not words, causing A3 sentence starter; B4 seeks happy memories, causing A5 options rather than bypass. The true option remains intentionally unanswered.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies partial memory and B4 offers a workable generic caption, prompting A to preserve the test instead.

heightening.evidence: B4 easy caption solution becomes A5 easier quiz format, still requiring remembered specifics.
